issue.title: Add a re-import regression check to sase-core's wheel-smoke and release-plz smoke steps
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-gg.4 (epic sase-gg) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; independently verified while landing that epic.

WHAT IS MISSING: sase-core's wheel-smoke CI job (crates/sase_core_py, .github/workflows/ci.yml) and the release-plz smoke step only exercise a plain 'import sase_core_rs'. That check passes even when the package init is broken in exactly the way that caused the sase-repo CI storm tracked by sase-fs, because the defect only surfaces on a RE-import while the compiled submodule stays cached.

THE DEFECT IT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT: maturin's generated sase_core_rs/__init__.py reads a bare 'sase_core_rs' on line 3 that the file never binds; it resolves only via importlib's cache-miss setattr(parent, child, module) side effect. Evicting or swapping the parent package while sase_core_rs.sase_core_rs stays cached makes the next import take the cache-hit path, skip that setattr, and raise 'NameError: name sase_core_rs is not defined', poisoning every later import in the process. Every published wheel through 0.18.4 carries this; the plain-import smoke never noticed across the entire release history.

REPRO (fails on published 0.18.4, passes on the PR #89 build):

    python -c "import sys, importlib; import sase_core_rs; del sys.modules['sase_core_rs']; importlib.import_module('sase_core_rs')"

SCOPE: add that eviction+re-import assertion to the wheel-smoke job and to the release-plz smoke step in sase-org/sase-core, so a regression in the package init is caught before a wheel is published to PyPI rather than by a downstream test suite.

ORDERING: land after sase-org/sase-core PR #89 ('fix(core-py): bind the extension module explicitly in the package init') merges — the check fails against the current package init by design, since that is the defect PR #89 fixes.

RELATED: sase-fs (the downstream symptom in this repo's CI); epic sase-gg (root cause + downstream containment). Distinct from both: this is a pre-existing gap in sase-core's own pre-publish gating, not caused by epic sase-gg, and its remediation lives in a different repo. sase-core work is tracked in this bead store by precedent (see sase-bh).
